correctness.rationale: On every nonempty concrete subalgebra of ([0,1], max, 1-x, max(0,2x-1)), the term *(neg(x∨neg x)) equals zero and forces preservation of 0 and 1. Define lambda=neg*neg and sigma=*: their scalar actions are clipping 2x and 2x-1. Iterating yields unary term ramps R_{k,j}(x)=[2^k x-j]_0^1 for all k>=0,0<=j<2^k. If a<j/2^k then R(a)=0 forces h(a)<=j/2^k; if (j+1)/2^k<a then R(a)=1 forces h(a)>=(j+1)/2^k. Density of dyadic cuts gives h(a)=a without continuity, injectivity, or finiteness assumptions. All maps therefore are inclusions, and S_n⊆S_m iff n divides m; singleton/endpoint cases are explicitly covered.

originality.rationale: The Coniglio--Esteva--Flaminio--Godo full paper gives detailed finite representability, skeleton structure, and componentwise embeddings (notably Proposition 5.9 and Theorem 5.16). That work is relevant and accounts for finite representable embeddings but it does not state a complete hom-set classification for *arbitrary*, including uncountable, concrete subalgebras, nor rule out all noninjective reduct-homomorphisms through dyadic term cuts. Full MV signature rigidity cannot simply be applied because this reduct is not always term-equivalent to MV-chains. Searches found no earlier equivalent full-category theorem; acknowledge potential implicit consequences of prior finite skeleton construction.
